what: Revit export of a hotel presidential suite, one plan per file (company 3D team, 9 Nov 2026)
floor_tag_note: tools/prims.py tags every item of a drawing it has no special case for with the cache name (one plan per file); all 29,886 items of prims.pkl carry area = 'suite_revit'
units_note: The DXF header says $INSUNITS = 1 (inches) and $MEASUREMENT = 0 (imperial); both are wrong. The geometry is in millimetres: the 'COLUMN_CONCRETE RECTANGLE_GEN - 500W 1000D' blocks measure 500 x 1000 units, the 'D22 1800X2100MM' double door has two 865-unit leaves with hinges 1,730 units apart, the 'D01_1000X2250MM' door a 930-unit swing, walls are 100-200 units thick. prims.py divides by 1000, so drawing metres are real metres.
extent_note: Extent of all geometry in model space (and of every item in prims.pkl, insert points excluded). The east edge x 25.079 and the south edge y 0.008-0.009 are the Revit view's crop: walls, two service double doors (x 24.02-25.75) and the leaves and arcs of two unit doors (y 0.81 down to 0.009) are cut there. Nothing lies outside this box in model space.
dxf_version: AC1032 (AutoCAD 2018 format), written by LibreDWG dwg2dxf
conversion_check: WORK/suite_revit/check_conversion.txt (made in the step before this one): every entity type count of the DXF equals LibreDWG's own dump of the DWG (all spaces and block definitions), hatch layers identical; only BLOCK/ENDBLK records differ, which are structure, not geometry

cache.not_in_cache: 1 WIPEOUT (skipped by prims.py); DIMENSION entities: none exist

frozen_note: frozen in the layer table (invisible in CAD) but present in the DXF and in prims.pkl
